Looking at the cuboid (3×2×2), I can track each colour:

- **Light grey piece:** the three top-front cubes plus the bottom-front-left cube — an L-shape.
- **Dark grey piece:** the bottom-front-middle, bottom-front-right, bottom-back-right cubes, plus the hidden bottom-back-middle cube — a 2×2 square block.
- **White piece:** the three top-back cubes plus the hidden bottom-back-left cube (the only remaining cube, since the dark grey piece needs the bottom-back-middle cube to stay connected).

So the white piece is a row of three cubes with one cube attached below the end — an L-shaped tetromino. Rotating option B (a column of three with one cube at the top end) gives exactly this shape.

\boxed{B}
